context.title: Civil War with Benjamin
context.summary: All Israel gathers at Mizpeh and demands that Benjamin hand over the men of Gibeah. Benjamin refuses, and war follows. Israel loses two battles, weeps before the Lord, and on the third day nearly wipes out Benjamin by an ambush.
context.background: 'From Dan even to Beer-sheba' (v. 1) means from the far north to the far south. The ark was then at 'the house of God' (in Hebrew, Bethel), with Phinehas, Aaron's grandson, serving before it (vv. 26–28). Benjamin's 700 left-handed slingers (v. 16) were feared; slings hurled stones with deadly force.

customs.term: Sling stones at an hair breadth
customs.note: A leather pouch on two cords, whirled and released. In skilled hands it was an accurate long-range weapon.

watchFor: The Levite's account leaves out his own part (vv. 4–7).
Israel asks God three times, with growing grief (vv. 18, 23, 26–28).
The ambush follows the same plan used at Ai (vv. 29–41).

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Dan
people.summary: The fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s maid (Gen. 30:6, “God hath judged me”, Heb. dananni).

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place.

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah.

people.name: Aaron
people.summary: The eldest son of Amram and Jochebed, a daughter of Levi (Ex. 6:20). Some explain the name as meaning mountaineer, others mountain of strength, illuminator.

people.name: Eleazar
people.summary: The third son of Aaron (Ex. 6:23). His wife, a daughter of Putiel, bore him Phinehas (Ex. 6:25). After the death of Nadab and Abihu (Lev. 10:12; Num. 3:4) he was appointed to the charge of the sanctuary (Num. 3:32).

people.name: Phinehas
people.summary: Son of Eleazar, the high priest (Ex. 6:25). While yet a youth he distinguished himself at Shittim by his zeal against the immorality into which the Moabites had tempted the people (Num. 25:1-9), and thus “stayed the plague” that had broken out among the people, and by which twenty-four thousand of them perished.

places.name: Beersheba
places.summary: Well of the oath, or well of seven, a well dug by Abraham, and so named because he and Abimelech here entered into a compact (Gen. 21:31). On re-opening it, Isaac gave it the same name (Gen. 26:31-33).

places.name: Dan
places.summary: The fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s maid (Gen. 30:6, “God hath judged me”, Heb. dananni).

places.name: Gilead
places.summary: Hill of testimony, (Gen. 31:21), a mountainous region east of Jordan. From its mountainous character it is called “the mount of Gilead” (Gen. 31:25).

places.name: Mizpah
places.summary: A city of Benjamin, “the watch-tower”, where the people were accustomed to meet in great national emergencies (Josh. 18:26; Judg. 20:1, 3; 21:1, 5; 1 Sam. 7:5-16).

places.name: Gibeah
places.summary: A hill or hill-town, “of Benjamin” (1 Sam. 13:15), better known as “Gibeah of Saul” (11:4; Isa. 10:29). It was here that the terrible outrage was committed on the Levite’s concubine which led to the almost utter extirpation of the tribe of Benjamin (Judg. 19; 20), only six hundred men surviving after a succession of disastrous battles.

places.name: Bethel
places.summary: A place in Central Palestine, about 10 miles north of Jerusalem, at the head of the pass of Michmash and Ai. It was originally the royal Canaanite city of Luz (Gen. 28:19).

places.name: Baal-tamar
places.summary: Lord of palm trees, a place in the tribe of Benjamin near Gibeah of Saul (Judg. 20:33). It was one of the sanctuaries or groves of Baal.

places.name: Rimmon
places.summary: “Rock of,” to which the Benjamites fled (Judg. 20:45, 47; 21:13), and where they maintained themselves for four months after the fearful battle at Gibeah, in which they were almost exterminated, 600 only surviving out of about 27,000.
